paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Saul and David get the same good news and take it two totally different ways. David "prospered in everything Saul sent him to do," and he did it because "the LORD was with him" (1 Samuel 18:5, 14). Saul looked at the same success and got afraid, because the LORD "was with David but had departed from Saul" (1 Samuel 18:12).

Now look at what jealousy does. It turns somebody else's win into your loss, and it makes you do things that make no sense. Saul, the KING, is scared of a man he put in charge himself, and every trap he sets ends up helping David (1 Samuel 18:15, 25-27). I've stood at the counter feeling sour because somebody else's cookies came out prettier, so I'm not pointing fingers, baker. I'm pointing at the oven.

Compare that to David. When Saul talks about marrying into the royal family, David asks, "Who am I?" and calls himself "a poor man and lightly esteemed" (1 Samuel 18:18, 23). Jonathan loves David "as himself" and hands over his own robe, with no jealous bone in him (1 Samuel 18:1, 4). So when somebody around you gets lifted up, you get to choose: clutch your spear or celebrate. And this story isn't over, so keep your oven warm.
